result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A labels every bar with its exact dollar value, highlights May lightly as the peak, and has a short source line, so it reads well in a newsletter. B is clean and correctly scaled, but readers have to estimate values from the $10k gridlines. It also has no source line, and its dark background suits a print newsletter less well. A's headline-style title and extra share-of-year sentence are a little more than asked for, but not enough to outweigh its clarity. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is easier to read: every bar has its dollar value, May stands out with a darker bar, it has a short source line, and the light background suits a newsletter. A is clean, accurate and simple. But it has no source line, its values can only be read roughly from the axis, and its dark theme is less suited to print. B's headline-style title and extra statistic in the subtitle go a little beyond the plain chart that was asked for.
